workingTitle: A solar shock wave strengthened far from its eruption
publicationStatus: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal Letters; preprint submitted October 22, 2026.
coreFacts: CHASE and SDO observed the X1.0 flare and 1086 km/s coronal mass ejection of October 2, 2022, together with a northward coronal EUV wave and chromospheric Moreton wave.
The EUV front moved at 788 plus or minus 21 km/s and the Moreton wave at 762 plus or minus 80 km/s.
After weakening, the Moreton wave Doppler redshift strengthened again about 213 plus or minus 15 megametres from the eruption.
A potential-field extrapolation located a coronal magnetic null about 70 megametres high near the enhancement, with a separatrix mapping down toward it.
SDO recorded a slower front initially moving at 151.3 km/s near the same location before it became nearly stationary.
A three-dimensional MHD simulation reproduced the propagating shock, stationary front, and enhanced hydrogen-alpha redshift; a control run without the null did not form the stationary front.
caveats: The direct measurement concerns one October 2, 2022 solar eruption; broader claims about common Moreton-wave behavior need additional events.
The magnetic null and mode conversion mechanism are inferred from field extrapolation plus a model constrained by the observations, not directly imaged as a conversion process.
The CHASE instrument raster-scans the solar disk, so the paper notes that the actual wave time within each raster can be tens of seconds later than the recorded scan start.
A possible contribution to coronal heating is not quantified and remains outside the study's scope.
